transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-24 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya (Velaris CTO), Liam (ML Eng), Sofia (Prod)

Summary: quick discovery on model selection. Focus on multilingual, long context (>=64k tokens target for some workflows), and tool-calling for retrieval + actions.

00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 45 minutes. I'll hand over to Priya for the deep parts but first, Maya, can you give a quick background on Velaris and the main goal here?
00:14 Maya (Velaris CTO): Sure, thanks Alex. Velaris builds a research assistant for climate data analysts. We ingest heterogeneous reports, sensor logs, a lot of multi-language text — english, spanish, portuguese, some french — and we need generation plus tool-calls to run queries back to our proprietary DB and trigger workflows. Main asks are: support for long context (a lot of docs per session), robust multilingual quality, and ability to call our internal tools safely. Also, data residency is a requirement for EU customers.
00:36 Alex: Great. Quick clarification — when you say long context, what ranges are we talking? 8k, 32k, 64k?
00:45 Liam (ML): For some analyst workflows we need close to 64k tokens of context — think multi-document transcripts plus sensor time series summaries. For most user sessions 32k would be OK but we want to support longer for the heavy cases.
01:02 Priya (Redwood SE): Got it. We do a few things for long-context: model selection (models that support extended context like Mistral-extended style or Llama variants), and runtime-level strategies — prefix caching, KV cache management, chunked retrieval. On Redwood Dedicated and Private we can tune runtime/kernel selection to favor long-seq performance; Hosted can also support it but there are tradeoffs on throughput and cost.
01:24 Maya: Could you give an example of tradeoffs?
01:27 Priya: Sure — on a hosted endpoint with a 64k model variant you'll see predictable latency for single requests but cost per token rises. On Dedicated you can provision GPUs with more memory and optimize batching to lower unit cost but you trade off the commit and management. Private gives you full control (VPC, KMS) for data residency but requires an enterprise install.
01:46 Sofia (Product): How about multilingual? We tried a few open models and quality in Portuguese dropped. Does Redwood recommend any particular family?
01:55 Priya: For multilingual, models trained on large diverse corpora tend to do better — Mistral-ish flavors and some of the Llama derivatives are strong. For Portuguese specifically, we've seen Mistral-Base/XL variants and some curated RedPajama-mix models for embeddings and generation perform better, but there's variability. We can benchmark with your sample docs. Also tokenization matters — effectiveness of subword tokenizers can change token counts and cost.
02:20 Liam: Tool-calling — we need secure function calls to our internal services, with auth, and a safe sandbox. Do you support function calling like OpenAI-style?
02:30 Alex: Yes, Redwood supports function/tool calling and structured outputs. Priya, maybe run through how we secure tool executions.
02:36 Priya: We support structured function calling in the API. For security on Hosted we provide per-request routing policies, allowlisting, and audit logs. For Dedicated/Private you can run the tool-exec within your VPC and use your KMS to protect keys. We also recommend an intermediary microservice that verifies and enforces auth scopes before executing actions.
02:58 Maya: Important for us is we can't allow models to exfiltrate keys or call arbitrary endpoints.
03:04 Priya: Totally — that's why the recommended pattern is a verifier layer plus RBAC and strict allowlists; we log every call and provide tracing in Console so you can see which model invoked which tool and with what payload.
03:20 Alex: Similar question — latency requirements? For interactive analyst workflows we want sub-2s for short prompts, but longer requests (64k) can be higher. Is that realistic?
03:30 Priya: Sub-2s for short prompts is achievable on Dedicated with optimized kernels and batching; on Hosted we have low-latency tiers but cost is higher. For 64k requests you're typically looking at higher latency — tens of seconds depending on compute and kernel. We can discuss streaming and progressive response patterns to keep UX snappy.
03:49 Maya: Security/compliance — we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), audit logs, and EU data residency. Which deployment is usually chosen for that?
03:58 Alex: Many customers choose Dedicated or Private for EU residency and strict compliance. Hosted can work if you have contracts and region controls, but Private gives you the most control. We'll send our SOC2 and the SSO integration guide.
04:12 Sofia: Any lock-in concerns with models? If we pick a Llama-based variant now and switch later, what does that look like?
04:20 Priya: The API is model-agnostic — you can pin model versions and switch with minimal code changes, but evaluation is key: output differences may require prompt tuning. Redwood Optimize gives model and quantization recommendations per workload.
04:34 Liam: About quantization — for Dedicated we plan to use int8 or q4 options to increase throughput. Does Redwood support those?
04:40 Priya: Yes, runtime supports quantized execution paths; kernel selection will prefer quant-friendly ops. We can recommend quant profiles per model.
04:48 Maya: Competitors — we did short tests with Anthropic and OpenAI's endpoints; Anthropic had strong safety but cost was higher; OpenAI had good latency. How does Redwood compare?
04:59 Alex: Redwood is a platform; we surface both curated open models and verified performance profiles. We can help choose a model family that balances cost/latency/quality and run side-by-side benchmarks.
05:12 Sofia: What's the next step?
05:14 Alex: Proposed next steps — we'll send a pricing + model comparison deck, security artifacts (SOC2, SAML guide), and Priya will prepare a benchmark plan to run on Hosted and on a Dedicated node if you want. Also, Maya, if you can share 10k tokens of anonymized sample content and a couple of representative prompts, we can run a quick POC.
05:33 Maya: Sounds good. We'll try to get samples by Monday.
05:36 Alex: Great. Any other concerns?
05:40 Maya: Just the cost/risk of trying multiple variants.
05:44 Priya: We often recommend starting Hosted for quick benchmarking, then move to Dedicated for production if you need throughput or residency. For Private we can schedule an enterprise scoping call.
05:55 Alex: Alright, I'll recap the action items after the call. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

Notes: occasional mis-transcription in automatic capture: "Mistral-ish" sometimes spelled "Mistral-ish" and product names like "Redwood Dedicated" may appear as "Red wood Dedicated". There was brief crosstalk at 02:30.

Recap / Next steps: see action items above.
